chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Muthanna al-Hannat from Abu Basir said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever prays four rak'at with two hundred recitations - saying 'Qul huwa Allahu Ahad' fifty times in each rak'ah - if there is any sin between him and Allah, Exalted and Glorious, it will be forgiven.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas fifty times in each of the four rak'at of prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on the Prayer of Necessity, this hadith highlights the immense spiritual efficacy of Surah Al-Ikhlas, equating its recitation to the weight of the entire Quran. The condition 'no sin remains between the servant and God' is interpreted by Shia scholars as referring to minor sins (hasanat), as major sins require specific repentance, emphasizing the purifying power of this specific dhikr.
